sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Metallic Minerals**: Minerals that contain raw metals in their uncombined state or as ores; they are malleable, ductile, possess metallic luster, and are good conductors of heat and electricity (e.g., Iron ore, Bauxite, Manganese).
• **Non-Metallic Minerals**: Minerals that do not contain extractable metals; they lack metallic luster, are brittle, poor conductors of electricity, and are often associated with sedimentary rock formations (e.g., Limestone, Mica, Gypsum, Dolomite).
• **Ferrous vs. Non-Ferrous Sub-classification**: Metallic minerals are further split into ferrous (containing iron, e.g., Iron, Manganese, Nickel) and non-ferrous (lacking iron, e.g., Copper, Lead, Zinc, Gold).
• **Key Metric / Factor**: Spatial concentration of minerals is dictated by geological eras, with metallic minerals predominantly found in ancient shield areas (Peninsular plateau) and non-metallic minerals in sedimentary basins.

items.definition: Naturally occurring solid material from which a metal or valuable mineral can be profitably extracted.
Accumulations of valuable minerals formed by gravity separation from a source rock during sedimentary processes (e.g., gold, diamond, platinum in river beds).
In major metallic minerals, smaller occurrences are called veins and larger are called lodes, formed when minerals are forced upwards through cracks in the crust and cool.

items.term: Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Act (MMDR Act, 1957)
items.definition: The principal legislation governing the mining sector in India, heavily amended in 2015, 2021, and 2023 to introduce transparent auctions and promote critical mineral exploration.

items.title: Major Geographical Distribution / Regional Hubs
items.content:
• **Chotanagpur Plateau & Odisha-Jharkhand Belt**: Hub for ferrous metallic minerals like Iron ore, Manganese, and Coal.
• **Rajasthan (Aravalli Belt)**: Major producer of non-ferrous minerals (Copper, Zinc, Lead) and non-metallic minerals (Limestone, Gypsum, Rock phosphate).

items.title: Challenges, Reforms & Forward Strategy
items.content:
• **Bottlenecks / Issues**: Illegal mining, environmental degradation, forest clearance hurdles, and heavy import dependence for critical minerals.
• **Policy Interventions**: National Mineral Policy, creation of Khanij Bidesh India Ltd (KABIL) for overseas acquisitions, and auction of 30 critical mineral blocks.

items.title: Mnemonic for Non-Metallic Minerals
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym / Phrase**: 'LMS-MGD' (Like My Science - Major Geological Deposits: Limestone, Mica, Salt, Magnesite, Gypsum, Dolomite).
• **Decoded Meaning**: Covers the most frequently asked non-metallic minerals in Prelims matching lists.
• **Prelims Exam Value**: Instantly eliminates options attributing metallic properties to minerals like Mica or Limestone.

items.title: Retention Rule of Thumb
items.content: • **Core Formula / Rule**: 'If it conducts heat/electricity and has luster = Metallic; If it makes cement, glass, or fertilizers = Non-Metallic (Sedimentary origin).'

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC frequently states that 'Mica is a metallic mineral because it is a good conductor of electricity.' Trap! Mica is a non-metallic mineral; although it has high dielectric strength and electrical resistance, it contains no metallic ores.

Mains Value Addition: In answers regarding industrial location, link the availability of metallic minerals in the Eastern Plateau region with the 'Resource Curse' paradox and sustainable tribal development under the DMF (District Mineral Foundation).

keyTakeaways: Metallic minerals are primarily igneous and metamorphic in origin, concentrated in peninsular cratons, while non-metallic minerals are largely sedimentary.
The MMDR Act and progressive amendments form the institutional backbone regulating mineral concessions and auctions in India.
Understanding the exact physical properties (malleability, conductivity) prevents negative marking in tricky Prelims exclusion questions.
